title: For injective L : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, (w, k) ↦ Lw + k is an isomorphism ℝ^d × (range L)^⊥ ≅ ℝ^P
statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ and let L : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be an injective linear map (automatically continuous, as ℝ^d is finite-dimensional). Let E := (range L)^⊥ ⊆ ℝ^P be the orthogonal complement of its range, with the subspace norm, and give ℝ^d × E the product (max) norm. Then there is a continuous linear equivalence Λ : ℝ^d × E → ℝ^P with Λ(w, k) = Lw + k for all w ∈ ℝ^d and k ∈ E.
lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (L : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P), Injective L → ∃ Λ : (Euclid d × ↥(L.range)ᗮ) ≃L[ℝ] Euclid P, ∀ (w : Euclid d) (k : ↥(L.range)ᗮ), Λ (w, k) = L w + k
